title: Shared LoReFT basis + many Mirror task codes
hypothesis: When task interventions cluster around a small number of shared representation-space modes, one shared LoReFT basis plus per-task Mirror mode codes will preserve intervention behavior with fewer actual bytes than independent low-rank interventions.
physical_object: one frozen 64D representation space and shared rank-4 LoReFT basis
mirror_coordinate: one discrete mode ID per task plus a shared intervention codebook
logical_multiplicity: 64 task-specific interventions generated from 8 latent intervention modes
controls: independent FP16 rank-4 LoReFT coordinates per task
shared 8-mode Mirror codebook plus task IDs

development.allowed: fit basis and 8-mode intervention codebook on development only; no fresh-dependent changes

success_gate: On every fresh world, Mirror NRMSE <=0.05 and total payload <=50% independent dense interventions, with no task-ID collisions that alter target function.
failure_gate: Discrete task codes collide or lose intervention quality, or FP16 shared coordinates match/better bytes at equal quality.
boundaries: Synthetic clustered interventions only; no pretrained Transformer or downstream NLP evidence.
Logical mode count is not capacity; task-wise function quality and interference determine utility.
